question: Discrimination of AD from MCI in ADNI from MRI: P-152 uses diffusion MRI (DTI features of the superficial white matter, ADNI2), P-301 uses T1 structural MRI (138 regional volumes through 3D vision transformers). The rule counts diffusion and structural MRI as one channel. Features, architecture, sample size and validation differ, which the rule allows. The record itself sets P-152's AD vs HC accuracy (95.8%) against P-301's AD vs MCI accuracy (0.74). Those are different contrasts (condition 6), so the pair is judged on the contrasts both papers print: AD vs MCI, MCI vs HC and AD vs HC.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy and AUC with AUC on each shared contrast. P-301's AD vs MCI AUROC (0.60) equals the balanced accuracy implied by its own accuracy (0.74), kappa (0.25) and class ratio, which suggests it is a single-operating-point value. Balanced accuracy is therefore compared as well, with P-152's taken from its printed sensitivity and specificity.

figures.P-301: AD vs MCI (deep-belief-network ensemble over 138 ROI 3D ViTs, single 80/20 split, results on the validation set): accuracy 0.74, AUROC 0.60, kappa 0.25 (Table 3). The validation n is not printed. 20% of the 364 AD+MCI scans is about 72 (23 AD/49 MCI). Wilson with n = 72: z^2/n = 0.0534, centre 0.728, half-width 0.0995 -> 0.628-0.827 (0.617-0.834 at n = 60). Hanley-McNeil with 23/49: Q1 = 0.6/1.4 = 0.429, Q2 = 2(0.36)/1.6 = 0.450, SE = sqrt([0.24 + 22(0.069) + 48(0.090)]/1127) = 0.073 -> 0.456-0.744. From accuracy 0.74, kappa 0.25 and an AD share of 0.32: expected agreement = 0.74 - 0.25(1 - pe) solved gives pe = 0.653, predicted-AD share (0.68 - 0.653)/0.36 = 0.074, true positives 0.067, sensitivity about 0.21, specificity about 0.99, balanced accuracy 0.60 (SE 0.5*sqrt(0.21*0.79/23 + 0.99*0.01/49) = 0.043 -> 0.515-0.684), equal to the printed AUROC. The other ensemble heads on the same task score AUROC 0.53-0.65 (Table 3), and adding demographics gives 0.58 (Table 6). CN vs MCI: 0.84 (n about 83: 0.746-0.904), AUROC 0.81 (Hanley-McNeil 34/49: 0.711-0.909). AD vs CN: 0.90 (n about 57: 0.795-0.954), AUROC 0.91.
figures.comparison: AD vs MCI: the AUCs exclude each other in both directions (0.60 below 0.853; 0.93 above 0.744), and so do the balanced accuracies (0.60 below 0.730; 0.835 above 0.684). The raw accuracies nearly overlap. 0.74 lies inside P-152's interval, and 0.833 lies 0.006 above P-301's derived upper bound (inside it at n = 60). That closeness comes from prevalence: P-301's model calls about 93% of a 68%-MCI set MCI. P-152's own sensitivity and specificity at P-301's 32% AD share give 0.32(0.807) + 0.68(0.863) = 0.845, outside 0.628-0.827. On MCI vs HC the papers agree on both metrics. AD vs HC is not compared because P-152's figure meets condition 5.

matched_figure_check: Neither paper reports AD vs MCI under the other's condition. P-152 has no T1 analysis and P-301 no diffusion analysis, and neither reports the other's class balance. P-301's alternative ensemble heads and its demographic-augmented model on the same task all stay at AUROC 0.53-0.65, so none of P-301's figures closes the gap. P-152 prints only its best kernel per contrast. The one contrast where both papers' figures agree (MCI vs HC) is a different comparison and does not reconcile AD vs MCI.
performance_validity: Passes on the compared figures. P-152's AD vs MCI AUC of 0.93 (48 subjects, internal 5-fold CV, no external cohort) is below 0.97, and P-301's figures are far below it. P-152's AD vs HC AUC of 0.99 on 48 subjects with internal CV only meets the Section 3.5 exclusion, but it is not a compared figure, the convention used for C-66 and C-117. P-152 runs FCBF feature selection before its 5-fold CV, which is the full-sample feature-selection design Section 3.5 names as a candidate mechanism. That design is recorded below as a candidate explanation, not as an exclusion.

candidate_explanations.difference: Features within the MRI channel: diffusion-tensor, tractography and connectivity features of the superficial white matter against T1 regional volumes.
candidate_explanations.quote: we applied an automated method to classify patients with AD and MCI and healthy control (HC) subjects based on the diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) features in the superficial white matter (SWM).

candidate_explanations.difference: Sample size and validation: 48 subjects per contrast, with feature selection done before an internal 5-fold CV, against a single 80/20 split of 364 AD+MCI scans.
candidate_explanations.quote: After feature selection, we performed an internal 5-fold cross-validation for the training data and applied the SVM algorithm using binary classification between the three groups.

candidate_explanations.difference: Class balance and operating point: balanced 24/24 in P-152 against 117 AD/247 MCI in P-301, where the derived sensitivity for AD is about 0.21.
candidate_explanations.quote: The baseline dataset includes 168 cognitively normal people (CN), 247 who have mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and 117 who have Alzheimer’s disease (AD).

candidate_explanations.difference: MCI composition: 57% of P-301's MCI group progresses within 24 months, which may bring it closer to AD. P-152 does not report the composition of its MCI group.
candidate_explanations.quote: further classified as 107 with stable MCI (sMCI) and 140 with progressive MCI (pMCI) based on their disease development over 24 months

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort subset: P-152 uses ADNI2 DTI participants only, and P-301 uses a baseline ADNI T1 dataset with two-year labels.
candidate_explanations.quote: were recruited from the ADNI2 project.

candidate_explanations.difference: Architecture: kernel SVM on selected features against a deep-belief-network ensemble over 138 per-region vision transformers.
candidate_explanations.quote: we propose the ROI-3DViT-DBN ensemble model for the early prediction of AD.

reason: The record's pairing misreads the contrasts (AD vs HC against AD vs MCI). On the contrast both papers print, AD vs MCI from MRI in ADNI, P-152's AUC 0.93 (0.853-1.000) and P-301's 0.60 (0.456-0.744) exclude each other, as do their balanced accuracies (0.835 vs 0.60), and neither compared figure is near ceiling. The raw accuracies nearly overlap only because P-301's model calls almost every case MCI in a 68%-MCI set: P-152's own class-wise figures at that ratio give 0.845, outside P-301's interval. The pair qualifies. The result rests on a derived validation n for P-301, and none of the candidate explanations (feature type within MRI, a 48-subject CV with feature selection before the folds, class balance, MCI composition, cohort, architecture) is shown to be sufficient.
